hard_case: Measured defect (#7558): ripr reported the related test's oracle `ensure!(score(2) != 0 || score(3) == 6)` as exact_value / strong, because one `==` anywhere in the condition credited the whole condition. RIPR-SPEC-0231 rule 1 (example 13 is the same ensure! inequality without the `||` arm): the disjunction passes whenever `score(2) != 0`, so the `== 6` arm pins nothing. The line verdict stayed gap because the owner pin is unconfirmed; the overclaim showed in the related test's reported oracle. Since #7558's fix ripr reports relational_check / weak.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: score(2) becomes 6, still nonzero, so the first disjunct holds and score(3) == 6 is never needed
not equivalent: score(2) and score(3) both become 0, so both disjuncts fail
not equivalent: score(2) becomes 0 and score(3) becomes 1, so both disjuncts fail

reasoning: ensure!(score(2) != 0 || score(3) == 6) (a local macro_rules! that returns Err) only rejects a zero score(2): x * 0 and x - 2 fail it, x * 3 passes. The `== 6` arm never pins the value because the first arm already holds.
